Hi Rishi,

Thanks for taking a look — quick one from our side as we scope a semantic search project. A few baseline questions so we can model cost:

- Do you price embeddings on a per-vector basis or per-token for hosted API? If per-vector, do you bill per request or per stored vector?
- What are your standard embedding dimensionalities and corresponding rate differences (e.g., 512 / 1536 / 3072)?
- Which hosted embedding models do you currently expose (names/brief perf notes)? Any open-source models offered through Redwood hosted endpoints?
- Do you offer committed-volume discounts or seat-based packaging for large vector counts? We are estimating ~12M active vectors stored and ~1M new vectors ingested monthly.
- Is there a bulk/async ingest flow and is that priced differently?

We need a simple sample calc (monthly) for 12M stored, 1M monthly ingest at 1536 dims and at 3072 dims. We may be open to an annual commit.

If you have a ratecard or a short spreadsheet that shows per-1k or per-vector pricing tiers, please attach.

Cheers,
Lena Park

Hi Lena — thanks for the clear list. Quick high-level answers and I attached a compact ratecard and a sample calc CSV. Happy to iterate after you confirm the exact dims and ingest pattern.

Summary (hosted API, list rates):
- Pricing units: we price embeddings primarily per-vector for hosted API; we show both per-vector and equivalent per-1k vectors on the ratecard. Tokenized per-token pricing is used for text-generation APIs, not embeddings.
- Standard dims & our typical list rates (list price per 1,000 vectors):
  * 512-d: $0.28 per 1k vectors (=$0.00028/vector)
  * 1,536-d: $0.60 per 1k vectors (=$0.00060/vector)
  * 3,072-d: $1.00 per 1k vectors (=$0.00100/vector)
- Models (hosted): rwd-emb-small (512), rwd-emb-standard (1536), rwd-emb-large (3072). We also host vetted open models (e.g., text-embed-3-like variants) for customers on request; availability depends on licensing and runtime profile.
- Billing notes: stored vectors are not billed separately beyond the per-vector inference cost unless you opt into our Storage Add-on for long-term retention/replication (that’s a storage fee). Ingest via our bulk async API is charged at the same per-vector inference rate; there is no separate bulk surcharge. Failed requests that return 4xx due to bad input are not billed; server-side 5xx retries are billed on successful attempts.

Attached: redwood-emb-ratecard-v2.xlsx (compact tiers) and sample-usage-calc.csv (I filled in the 12M / 1M scenarios).

If you are considering an annual committed contract at ~12M active vectors and 1M monthly ingestion, we can put together a committed discount structure. What’s your preferred procurement cadence — 12 months or multi-year?

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Thanks for the context — see proposed commercial package below and a recommended line to include on the draft quote. I attached a one-page draft quote (DW_Draft_Quote_2026-11-04.pdf) to share with procurement once you ok the numbers.

Proposed package (Hosted + Storage Add-on) — 12-month committed term, billing monthly:
- List rates (for reference): 1,536-d = $0.60 / 1k vectors; 3,072-d = $1.00 / 1k vectors.
- Committed pricing (12M active vectors, 1M monthly ingest):
  * 1,536-d: $0.45 per 1k vectors (25% off list) -> effective $5,400/month for 12M vectors active (metered at active count) + $450/month for monthly ingestion of 1M vectors (metered as 1M * per-vector) — note: we bill inference on ingest; storage add-on below covers long-term retention.
  * 3,072-d: $0.70 per 1k vectors (30% off list) -> effective $8,400/month + $700/month for the 1M monthly ingest.
- Storage Add-on (optional): $50 per 1M vectors per month (covers replicated storage, index snapshots, and retention tooling). For 12M active vectors: $600/month.
- Billing unit: invoiced per 1k vectors with metering granularity at 1k. We include a quarterly usage reconciliation. Failed 4xx calls not billed; retries counted on success.
- Dedicated availability: rwd-emb-large (3,072-d) is available on Dedicated; if they go Dedicated there is a different pricing pool and we can include capacity pricing in a follow-up.

Commercial notes / recommended playbook:
- Present the 25% / 30% off list as the committed discount because it’s simple and easy for procurement to evaluate.
- Offer a 30/60/90 day pilot at list rate with a credit applied to the first invoice if they sign the 12-month contract. That lowers friction for engineering to validate quality.

Next steps: Rishi — if you’re okay, send the attached one-page quote and include the sample calc CSV when you engage procurement. I’ll draft a HubSpot deal line item and push the quote to the HubSpot link below.
